Find intersections of y=x^2 and y=9.
Set x^2=9, so x=+/-3 and y=9.
The equation (x+1)^2=0 has a repeated root.
Factor x^2-6x+8=(x-2)(x-4), then use the line.
Find p such that y=x^2+px+4 is tangent to y=2x; give each point.
The discriminant (p-2)^2-16=0 gives p=6 or -2. Substitute each repeated root.
